title: Eliminate the semiconductor channel: NEM contact relay access switch
idea: Remove the transistor channel altogether and isolate each storage node with a nanoelectromechanical cantilever relay whose off state is a 5-10 nm air gap. The wordline electrostatically pulls the beam into contact for read/write; once released there is no subthreshold, junction or GIDL path, only gap tunneling (<1e-24 A).
why: Attacks the 13 fA leakage tail and refresh (fact 3): retention is bounded only by capacitor dielectric leakage, so refresh interval moves from 64 ms to minutes, removing most of the ~46 fJ/bit refresh energy and 10-20% bandwidth loss. Contact wear threatens unlimited endurance.

title: Eliminate refresh for ephemeral data: lifetime-tagged no-refresh DRAM regions
idea: Software tags allocations with a maximum lifetime (activations, gradients, KV-cache blocks consumed within milliseconds); the controller maps them to banks with refresh disabled, and a per-region epoch timer faults if data outlives the guaranteed retention bin. Data that dies before it decays is never refreshed.
why: AI activation traffic often lives <10-50 ms; removing refresh for 30-60% of HBM capacity eliminates the 16-33% idle-power refresh share and 10-20% bandwidth loss on those banks with no cell change.

title: Eliminate dopants: polarization-induced 2DEG GaN access transistor
idea: Replace the doped Si access device with an AlGaN/GaN heterostructure whose channel electrons come from spontaneous and piezoelectric polarization rather than dopants, turned off with a recessed p-GaN gate. No implant, no random dopant fluctuation and a 3.4 eV gap remove the junction and thermal-generation leakage tail.
why: Intrinsic carrier density ~1e-10 cm^-3 vs 1e10 in Si; leakage could fall >1000x, pushing retention to seconds and removing most refresh energy; GaN-on-Si is an existing U.S. power-electronics process. Array-density integration is unproven.

title: Eliminate the storage-node junction: electrostatically induced virtual drain
idea: Delete the n+ storage-node implant: a thin, always-biased spacer gate (polarity gate) induces an electron layer that acts as the drain, so there is no metallurgical junction under the gate edge for band-to-band tunneling. The storage node contacts the induced layer through a silicide.
why: GIDL and junction trap-assisted tunneling dominate the retention tail (fact 3); removing the junction field peak could cut tail leakage 10-100x and stretch the refresh period 4-10x.

title: Eliminate explicit refresh for weights re-read every inference pass
idea: The controller keeps a per-row touched-this-window bit; in LLM serving, where weight rows are streamed every token (<20-50 ms), rows proven read within tREFW get REF suppressed because each activation already restores the cells. A watchdog issues REF only to rows the access pattern missed.
why: Weight-streaming inference touches most of HBM per token; suppressing redundant refresh recovers ~10-20% bandwidth and ~46 fJ/bit refresh energy across the weight footprint.

title: Eliminate the leakage tail: per-cell Vt trim via charge-trap back gate
idea: Give each access transistor a thin back gate with a nitride charge-trap layer; at final test the tester finds the leakiest 0.1-1% of cells and Fowler-Nordheim-programs electrons into their back-gate trap, raising Vt 200-300 mV permanently. The tail cells that set the refresh rate are trimmed to the median.
why: Refresh interval is set by the worst ~1e-6 of cells; collapsing the tail by 1-2 decades lets tREFW stretch 4-16x, cutting refresh energy and bandwidth loss proportionally (fact 3).

title: Eliminate the Boltzmann limit: feedback-FET access device
idea: Use a gated p-i-n feedback FET whose intrinsic region holds charge barriers that collapse abruptly under positive feedback, giving <1 mV/dec switching. The device is hard off at 0 V gate and fully on near 1 V, so the 3 V wordline and the negative-wordline pump are removed.
why: Breaks the voltage floor (fact 10) and the leakage-vs-on-current tradeoff: ~1e-18 A off current at equal on current, wordline energy ~9x lower (3 V to 1 V), pump periphery area removed (fact 7).

title: Eliminate the worst-case guard band: deliberately leaky canary cells
idea: Embed a few sentinel cells per subarray built with intentionally shortened access transistors so they leak 4-8x faster than any real cell; a tiny comparator watches them and refreshes that subarray only when a canary crosses threshold. Refresh then tracks real temperature, voltage and aging instead of the 64 ms worst-case spec.
why: Most rows retain for seconds; replacing the fixed worst-case schedule with measured leakage cuts refresh operations 4-10x at typical temperatures, recovering most of the 16-33% idle-power share.

title: Eliminate sensing during refresh: node-gated broadcast recharge pulse
idea: Add a small second transistor whose gate is the storage node, linking the node to a shared restore line; a bank-wide pulse on that line tops up every node holding '1' (transistor on) and leaves '0' nodes untouched (transistor off). Refresh becomes one global pulse with no row activation, sense amplifiers or bitline swing.
why: Refresh energy drops from ~46 fJ/bit to a few fJ/bit (no bitline CV^2, no sensing) and refresh no longer blocks banks, recovering 10-20% bandwidth; costs ~30% cell area.

title: Eliminate resistance: superconducting persistent-current loop cryogenic memory tier
idea: Store each bit as a clockwise or counter-clockwise persistent current in a superconducting NbN loop, accessed through a kinetic-inductance nanowire switch briefly driven normal by a write pulse. A persistent current never decays, so there is no leakage and no refresh; deploy as a 4 K tier beside superconducting or quantum compute.
why: Zero static leakage, fJ-level switching, refresh removed entirely; niobium thin films need no EUV. Density is limited by loop inductance (~1 um^2 cells) and cryo overhead.

title: Eliminate static storage: bistable Duffing MEMS resonators sustained by pump
idea: Each bit is the high- or low-amplitude branch of a nonlinear (Duffing) silicon-nitride nanomechanical resonator; one shared parametric pump tone keeps every resonator on whichever branch it occupies, so state is held by the pump, not by isolated charge. Writes kick a resonator between branches; reads sense amplitude capacitively.
why: Removes leakage-driven decay and per-row refresh (fact 3): retention is unlimited while the pump runs at ~aJ per resonator per cycle, from EUV-free SiN MEMS processing.

title: Eliminate gate electrostatics: piezoelectric transduction switch as access device
idea: Replace the FET with a piezoelectronic transistor: a relaxor piezoelectric (PMN-PT) actuator squeezes a thin piezoresistive SmSe layer, driving an insulator-to-metal transition with 1e4-1e5 resistance change at ~0.1 V. The off state is a wide-gap insulator rather than a thermally populated channel.
why: Sub-0.2 V switching attacks the 1 V/3 V voltage floor (fact 10) and the insulating off state could cut leakage by orders of magnitude; materials integration risk is very high.

title: Eliminate the solid channel: vacuum nanogap field-emission access transistor
idea: Isolate each storage node with a 10-20 nm vacuum gap between a sharpened emitter tip and collector, gated by a surrounding electrode; electrons cross only by field emission when the gate thins the barrier. With no semiconductor there is no thermal generation, GIDL or subthreshold conduction.
why: Off current ~1e-21 A lets the capacitor dielectric set retention (minutes+); temperature-immune, ideal for hot AI packages where Si leakage doubles every ~10 C.

title: Eliminate refresh of unallocated memory: OS free-page refresh mask
idea: The OS page allocator exports a free/zeroed-page bitmap to the memory controller over a CXL or DDR mode-register channel; rows holding only free pages are excluded from refresh and zero-filled on reallocation. Servers commonly leave 20-50% of DRAM unallocated or as droppable clean cache.
why: Removes 20-50% of refresh operations fleet-wide with no cell change, saving idle power and bandwidth at 32-64 Gb densities.

title: Eliminate yield loss from retention: sell short-retention dies to streaming customers
idea: Bin dies that fail 64 ms retention but pass 8-16 ms and sell them at a discount into weight-streaming inference appliances whose firmware runs 4-8x refresh or proves per-pass re-reads. Dies now scrapped or patched with redundancy become supply.
why: Raises usable DRAM bit supply a few percent up to ~10% per wafer during a 4x price shock without new fabs (capital intensity).

title: Eliminate the one-size retention spec: per-die retention descriptor standard
idea: Propose a JEDEC extension in which each die stores its measured retention distribution (per bank, per temperature) in an on-die fuse table and the host sets tREFI per bank from it; validated dies advertise 128-512 ms classes. The single worst-case 64 ms contract disappears.
why: Most dies retain far longer than spec; per-die refresh rates cut refresh power and bandwidth loss 2-8x industry-wide with zero fab capital.

title: Eliminate refresh of read-only copies: re-fetch from durable backing store
idea: Read-only data (weights, embeddings) is mapped to never-refreshed banks with strong per-line ECC; when ECC flags drift the line is re-fetched from a NAND or CXL pool that holds the master copy, and a scrubber rewrites lines nearing their measured retention age. Refresh becomes on-demand repair.
why: Refresh energy and bandwidth fall to near zero for the read-only majority of inference memory, trading rare microsecond re-fetches for constant refresh.

title: Eliminate electronic charge storage: solid-electrolyte proton-intercalation bit
idea: Store the bit as protons intercalated into a 5 nm WO3 channel, written through a thin inorganic proton conductor (e.g., hydrogenated HfO2) with ~10 ns pulses; at zero bias the ions are immobile, so nothing leaks, and reads measure channel conductance non-destructively. Electrons are not the stored quantity, so they cannot leak away.
why: Eliminates refresh and destructive read (facts 3, 8); open risks are ionic-cycling endurance and speed versus DRAM's unlimited-endurance target.

title: Eliminate charged cells: inversion encoding plus refresh skip for discharged rows
idea: Each row stores a 1-bit inversion flag chosen at write time so most cells sit in the discharged, non-leaking state; rows whose cells are all discharged (zero pages, sparse activations, quantized weights' high bits) are flagged and skipped by refresh.
why: AI tensors are 30-70% zero or sparse; skipping such rows and halving charged cells elsewhere cuts refresh count 30-50% and lowers row-hammer exposure (fact 9).

title: Eliminate ground dumping: resonant LC adiabatic bitline refresh
idea: During refresh, drive bitline restore from an on-package resonant LC tank (thin-film inductors in the interposer) so charge sloshes between banks instead of being dumped to ground; sense amplifiers only steer the resonant swing. Roughly 60-80% of bitline CV^2 is recovered each refresh cycle.
why: Refresh energy ~46 fJ/bit could drop to ~10-20 fJ/bit, attacking the CV^2 floor (fact 10) without changing the cell.

title: Eliminate the three-terminal transistor: threshold-switch selector 1S1C crosspoint DRAM
idea: Isolate each capacitor with a two-terminal volatile threshold switch (OTS or NbO2 Mott selector) stacked directly on it in a crosspoint, addressed by V/2 biasing; no wordline transistor and no lateral device, so tiers stack like 3D crosspoint.
why: Removes the 3D DRAM lateral-transistor blocker (fact 2) and enables 4F^2 stacking; half-select leakage must reach <1e-15 A for even millisecond retention, hence high risk.

title: Eliminate room temperature: 77 K liquid-nitrogen DRAM tier
idea: Run a DRAM pool immersed in liquid nitrogen, where junction and subthreshold leakage fall >1e6x so refresh disappears, and redesign access transistors with low Vt so the wordline drops from 3 V to ~1 V. Pair with cryo-CMOS controllers; LN2 is cheap and helium-free.
why: Refresh eliminated, wordline energy ~9x lower, relaxed Vt allows smaller devices; avoids the helium chokepoint. Cooling overhead (~10 W per W removed) limits it to large pools.

title: Eliminate single-device isolation: stacked series access transistors exploiting stack effect
idea: Replace the single access FET with two series vertical FETs sharing one gate; in the off state the middle node floats up, giving the upper device negative Vgs and reduced Vds (the logic stack effect) and cutting subthreshold leakage ~10x. Vertical stacking keeps the 4F^2 footprint.
why: ~10x lower leakage gives ~10x longer refresh period with known silicon processing (fact 3).

title: Eliminate per-cell access transistors: CCD recirculating memory from university nanofab
idea: Build a three-phase surface-channel CCD (two poly levels, 2 um contact lithography, standard university processing) in which data circulate as charge packets past a regenerating sense stage each lap; no cell has its own access transistor or junction leak path, and each lap is the refresh. Target streaming weight memory where access is sequential anyway.
why: Removes the per-bit access device and most periphery; dark-current-limited retention plus regeneration each lap; EUV-free and demonstrable in a university fab within months.

title: Eliminate refresh with bistable Goto-pair tunnel-diode cell
idea: Make silicon interband tunnel diodes with spin-on dopants and rapid thermal anneal, and series-connect two of them (a Goto pair) at the storage node so their NDR curves create two stable voltages; one access FET writes the node. The cell holds state statically at nA standby current, so refresh is eliminated.
why: Static retention near DRAM density (three devices, vertical diodes) removes refresh energy and bandwidth loss (fact 3); standby current must stay <1 nA/cell.

title: Eliminate the semiconductor: ALD MIIM tunnel-diode 1D1C cell
idea: Isolate each capacitor with a metal-insulator-insulator-metal diode (ALD Al2O3/Ta2O5 between dissimilar work-function metals) whose step-tunneling barrier gives ~1e6 nonlinearity; cells are crosspoint-addressed by V/2 biasing, and at hold bias tunneling is exponentially suppressed. Every layer is a university ALD or sputter step.
why: No crystalline silicon or dopants, BEOL-stackable for many tiers (fact 2); retention hinges on reaching <1e-17 A at half-select.

title: Eliminate the channel: volatile Ag/Ag2S gap-type atomic switch access
idea: Use a gap-type atomic switch: a 1-2 nm vacuum gap between an Ag2S electrode and a Pt counter electrode, where a gate pulse grows a single-atom Ag bridge for access and the bridge dissolves spontaneously when bias is removed. The off state is a true vacuum gap with tunnel leakage below 1e-20 A.
why: Retention set only by capacitor dielectric, so refresh is eliminated; built with e-beam lithography and evaporation in any university fab; endurance and speed are open risks.

title: Eliminate thermal generation: 4H-SiC MOS dynamic memory cell
idea: Build 1T1C cells on purchased 4H-SiC epi wafers with NO-annealed thermal oxide and an npn or MOS access device; with a 3.26 eV gap the thermal generation rate is ~1e-17 of silicon's, so stored charge lasts hours or longer at room temperature, as early academic SiC test cells showed. University fabs already process SiC power devices.
why: Refresh essentially eliminated (fact 3) and cells tolerate hot packages; U.S. SiC wafer supply exists; density and cost per bit are the challenge.

title: Eliminate the gate oxide: exfoliated beta-Ga2O3 Schottky-gate MESFET access
idea: Exfoliate or pattern beta-Ga2O3 nanomembranes and gate them directly with a Ni/Au Schottky gate, so there is no gate dielectric and no oxide or interface traps to cause random-telegraph leakage or variable retention time. The 4.8 eV gap gives aA-class off current.
why: Removes the trap-assisted tail behind refresh (fact 3); needs only e-beam lithography and evaporation; gallium avoids the W/He chokepoints.

title: Eliminate deposited dielectrics: Bi2O2Se channel with native Bi2SeO5 gate oxide
idea: Grow 2D Bi2O2Se by CVD and partly convert it with UV-ozone or O2 plasma into its native high-k (k~20) Bi2SeO5, forming a Si/SiO2-like clean interface on an atomically thin body; the access device reaches near-60 mV/dec swing with full depletion. All steps are tube-furnace and plasma steps.
why: Atomically thin, trap-free channel shrinks GIDL and trap leakage and is vertically stackable (facts 2-3).

title: Eliminate bulk thickness: 2 nm quantum-confined silicon body widens bandgap
idea: Thin SOI by repeated thermal oxidation and HF strip to a 2-3 nm body, where quantum confinement widens silicon's effective gap by ~0.3-0.5 eV and suppresses intrinsic carrier density 1e3-1e4x; build the access device in this film over a thick buried oxide. Only furnace oxidation and wet etch are needed.
why: Leakage drops ~1000x from bandgap widening while staying all-silicon and U.S.-manufacturable; mobility loss is tolerable because a cell needs only microamps.

title: Eliminate the substrate body: XeF2-released suspended nanowire gate-all-around access device
idea: Pattern Si nanowires by e-beam lithography, undercut them with XeF2 vapor so they hang free, then wrap them with ALD HfO2/TiN to form a gate-all-around access device with no body contact and no junction to substrate. The storage node connects only to the suspended wire.
why: Removes the junction-to-substrate leakage component and lowers DIBL, cutting off current 10-100x vs recessed-channel devices; all steps are standard university nanofab.

title: Eliminate implant damage: molecular monolayer doping for access junctions
idea: Form storage-node and bitline junctions by grafting a phosphorus- or arsenic-bearing molecular monolayer onto silicon, capping it and driving in by rapid thermal anneal, giving ultra-shallow junctions with no ion-implant end-of-range defects. Implant-induced deep traps are a key source of the trap-assisted junction leakage tail.
why: Fewer deep-level traps tighten the retention tail (fact 3) and remove the need for an implanter (capital); wet chemistry plus RTA only.

title: Eliminate plasma-etch damage: KOH crystallographic (111) sidewall vertical channel
idea: Define vertical access-transistor channels by anisotropic KOH/TMAH etching of (110) silicon so channel sidewalls are atomically flat (111) planes instead of plasma-roughened surfaces, then grow thermal gate oxide. Lower interface-state density and no etch damage remove generation and VRT centers.
why: Interface traps drive trap-assisted tunneling and variable retention; 5-10x lower Dit narrows the retention tail (fact 3) with cheap wet etching.

title: Eliminate lithography: block-copolymer self-assembled pillars for vertical access transistors
idea: Spin a PS-b-PMMA block copolymer, anneal it into a hexagonal 20-30 nm pitch pattern, transfer it into silicon as vertical pillars, and build surrounding-gate access transistors whose channel length is set by etch depth (long, low-leakage), not lithography. Only contact lithography is used for coarse alignment.
why: Removes EUV from the access-device level (fact 4) and allows long vertical channels in a 4F^2 footprint, lowering leakage; registration and defectivity are the risk.

title: Eliminate shared thermal budgets: transfer-printed silicon nanomembrane access transistors
idea: Fabricate access transistors in SOI nanomembranes with full high-temperature processing, release them, and transfer-print them with an elastomer stamp onto a separately built high-k capacitor backplane. Neither part must survive the other's anneal, so junctions stay pristine and the capacitor gets its crystallization anneal.
why: Decoupling processes avoids anneal-induced leakage degradation and opens heterogeneous stacking toward 3D (fact 2); print alignment limits density.

title: Eliminate permanent tail cells: in-field Joule self-heating anneal of traps
idea: Drive a short high-current pulse through each gate-all-around nanowire access device, or use its wordline as a resistive heater, to reach ~500-700 C locally for microseconds and re-passivate the defects that cause variable retention time. Repeat periodically in the field to heal aging-induced leakage.
why: Heals the tail cells that dictate refresh, shrinking tail leakage ~10x (fact 3); demonstrable on university-fab nanowires with a probe station.

title: Eliminate heat-driven leakage: thin-film Bi2Te3 Peltier cooler under array
idea: Sputter or co-evaporate thin-film Bi2Te3/Sb2Te3 thermoelectric couples into the substrate or interposer beneath the memory array, pumping the cell region 15-25 C below the surrounding logic. Since leakage roughly doubles per ~10 C, cooling only the array extends retention 3-6x.
why: Refresh energy and bandwidth loss fall 3-6x in hot HBM stacks beside GPUs; thin-film thermoelectrics are university processes; costs some Peltier power.

title: Eliminate the 3 V wordline: negative-capacitance HZO access gate
idea: Insert an ALD Hf0.5Zr0.5O2 ferroelectric layer, capacitance-matched to an HfO2/SiO2 underlayer, into the access gate so it acts as an internal voltage amplifier with sub-60 mV/dec slope. The same off current is reached with a 1-1.5 V wordline swing, or the same swing gives ~100x lower leakage.
why: Wordline CV^2 energy cut 4-9x (fact 10) and charge-pump area removed (fact 7); hysteresis-free matching is the risk.

title: Eliminate leakage pathways: Coulomb-blockade-locked silicon nanodot storage node
idea: Store a small charge on a 2-3 nm Si nanodot (LPCVD-grown or e-beam defined) that gates a sense FET and is separated from the bitline by a tunnel barrier; the >100 meV Coulomb charging energy blocks single-electron escape at hold bias, exponentially suppressing leakage. A write gate lowers the barrier.
why: Retention could exceed seconds with non-destructive gain-transistor reads (facts 3, 8); room-temperature blockade needs sub-3 nm uniformity.

title: Eliminate the doped storage-node junction: high-barrier PtSi Schottky contact
idea: Replace the n+ storage-node junction with a self-aligned PtSi or IrSi contact on n-type silicon (barrier ~0.85-0.95 eV), forming a gate-modulated Schottky-barrier access device; in hold, the barrier blocks thermionic emission and there is no junction depletion region to host trap-assisted generation. Silicidation runs below 500 C.
why: Removes the implanted-junction leakage component and yields BEOL-compatible access devices for stacking (facts 2-3); evaporation and furnace only.

title: Eliminate the incumbents' data monopoly: open 1-um access-device PDK across universities
idea: Publish an open process kit for 100 mm wafer access devices (Si, SiC, Ga2O3 variants) runnable in ten U.S. university nanofabs, each running monthly shuttles with standardized retention-tail test structures; pooled data on millions of cells reveal which elimination (junction, oxide, body) shrinks the tail.
why: Breaks the barrier that only three firms see leakage-tail statistics at scale; accelerates U.S. access-device innovation for ~$10M/yr instead of a $15B fab.

title: Eliminate the wordline wire: light-gated wide-bandgap photoconductive access switch
idea: Replace the electrical wordline with a SiN waveguide row that delivers a nanosecond UV or blue pulse to ZnO or GaN photoconductive switches at each cell; in the dark the wide-gap switch has essentially no carriers and no leakage. The waveguide is passive, so wordline RC delay and 3 V pumps disappear.
why: Removes wordline drivers and high-voltage pumps (facts 7, 10) plus the leakage tail; SiN waveguides and sputtered ZnO are university processes; optical energy per access is the risk.

title: Eliminate the solid gate dielectric: air-gap suspended-gate FET
idea: Fabricate a suspended metal gate over the channel on a sacrificial amorphous-Si layer released by XeF2; the gate pulls in electrostatically for access with abrupt switching and springs back to a large air gap in hold, deepening the off state and removing gate-oxide traps. Unlike a contact relay, current still flows through a semiconductor channel.
why: Steep switching cuts wordline voltage and leakage together (facts 3, 10); sacrificial MEMS release is routine in university fabs; stiction and speed are risks.

title: Eliminate thermionic injection: Ge/Si heterojunction tunnel FET access device
idea: Build a vertical tunnel FET with a CVD-grown p+ Ge source on an n-type Si channel so carriers enter only by band-to-band tunneling; at hold bias the tunneling window closes and there is no thermionic tail, giving ~1e-18 A/um off current. The low on current is fine because one cell needs only microamps.
why: Leakage 100-1000x below MOSFET access devices at equal gate bias, enabling ~10x longer refresh intervals; university CVD plus RTA.

title: Eliminate inter-cell dielectric: air-gap isolation against passing-gate leakage
idea: Replace STI oxide between adjacent cells with sealed air-gap trenches (sacrificial poly removed by XeF2, sealed by PECVD), so passing wordlines couple far less into neighbouring storage nodes and no trapped oxide charge sits at the isolation edge.
why: Passing-gate effects and STI-edge traps feed the retention tail and row hammer (facts 3, 9); k=1 vs 3.9 cuts coupling ~4x using standard university MEMS steps.
